name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502, 2023.
rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in three stages: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format with necessary corrections. (3) Authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects covered by the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and is instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark aims to evaluate models on tasks akin to those faced by experts, with potential implications for job displacement and economic disruption as models approach the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor.
rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, but this may not capture all aspects of expert-level reasoning. Additionally, the benchmark may not represent a sufficient test for Expert AGI as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI should tackle.
rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is designed for testing and validation of large multimodal models. It is intended to evaluate models' capabilities in expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across diverse disciplines. The benchmark should be used to assess both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities in professional domains. It is not recommended for training purposes due to its limited size and focus on evaluation.
